records.name: Zigurds
records.facts_used: Catalogue refers Zigurds to the Sigurd entry (p. 290): Old Norse sigr “victory”, varðōn “to guard”, Sighurdher “guardian of victory”; first quarter of the 20th century; calendar 1915 (pp. 338; 290).
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: The referenced entry’s headword is reported with long ū (Sigūrds); history phrases it as the Scandinavian Sigurd entry. German Sigurd → Zīgurds (Ceplītis 1960, LVA) has long ī and is not used as an exact bridge. Siliņš catalogue pages are attributed online transcriptions, not newly inspected printed pages. Original PDF pages were visually read where cited.

records.name: Sigurds
records.facts_used: LVA export visually checked: Swedish Sigurd → Sigurds, Elsberga, LVKJ 21 (1985) p. 111 (separate Balode 2003 p. 324 row gives Sīgurds). SNL signed Alhaug: Old Norse Sig-urðr, “siger” + “vaktar”; Bjørnson plays Sigurd Slembe (1862), Sigurd Jorsalfar (1872); Sigurd Jorsalfare 1090–1130.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: The 1985 article itself was not inspected; the agency row is the accepted bridge. Norwegian episodes are labelled Norwegian. Siliņš catalogue says its entry is long-ū Sigūrds; Norwegian manual gives Sigurs (NORDIC03 PDF 116 / printed 220); German gives Zīgurds. None of their dates are transferred.

records.name: Jaunutis
records.facts_used: Salys PDF 109 / printed 94: Jaunutis same affectionate diminutive formation as Kęstutis; PDF 48 / printed 33: baptised Ivan, 1345 in Moscow. VLE Jaunutis: grand duke 1342–early 1345, baptised Jonas in Moscow 1345-09. Guide: from Jaunius < jaunas.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: VLE says Jono vardu; Salys gives Ivan — both reported with attribution. 1964 calendar PDF 314 / printed 299: Jaunutis (Jaunis) 25 September, differs from project 25 January; project date preserved.

records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Frequency ratios on the same page not used. Leole Dec 2005 gloss not used.

records.name: Paavel
records.facts_used: Rajandi PDF 140 / printed 142: Pavel ~ Paavel → Paul; Estonian Paavel among forms. Mägiste PDF 44 / printed 42: [Paavel -li (KA Pawell, TLAV IV 84, SB 1927 124, P 128 Pawel, KKVA 50 Pauel …) = Paul(us)]; abbreviations PDF 11 / printed 9: P = Polska XVI wieku, Inflanty; KKVA = Keila churchwardens’ account book 1472–1553.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Mägiste prints the entry in square brackets; the bracket convention was not interpreted. Older spellings are family records, not Paavel first attestations. EE-TURK10 p. 82 farm-name note not used.

records.name: Paavo
records.facts_used: Rajandi PDF 140 / printed 142: Finnish Paavo, Estonian Paavel/Paavo/Paul; PDF 60 / printed 62: some South Estonian Paavo possibly from Fabian. Mägiste PDF 44 / printed 42: Paavo (P 247 Pawe Laur …; cf. Finnish Paavo = Paavel).
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Both routes kept; no bearer-specific route asserted. Pawe record is not the modern spelling.

records.name: Paap
records.facts_used: Mägiste PDF 44 / printed 42: Paap -bu (P 109, 210 Pap; cf. Paul; Wd. Paabu, Paapu women’s names). Rajandi PDF 140 / printed 142: reduplication of Paul view (Mägiste) vs probable Fabian origin; PDF 60 / printed 62: South Estonian Paabo ~ Paabu ~ Paap based on Fabian.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Origin explicitly disputed and presented as such; not resolved. Leole Dec 2005 “Latin small” gloss for Paap rejected (conflicts with Rajandi).
